MI300X.Address Processing Unit and Data Return: Percent of the total CU cycles the address processor was busy
Percent of the total CU cycles the address processor was stalled from sending address requests further into the vL1D pipeline.
Percent of the total CU cycles the address processor was stalled from sending write/atomic data further into the vL1D pipeline.
Percent of total CU cycles the address processor was stalled waiting to send command data to the data processor.
The number of cycles the sequencer was stalled waiting to send address requests to the address processor due to a full address FIFO, per normalization unit.
The number of cycles the sequencer was stalled waiting to send commands to the address processor due to a full command FIFO, per normalization unit.
The number of cycles the sequencer was stalled waiting to send write data to the address processor due to a full data FIFO, per normalization unit.
The total number of global & generic memory atomic (with and without return) instructions executed on all compute units on the accelerator, per normalization unit.
The total number of global & generic memory instructions executed on all compute units on the accelerator, per normalization unit.
The total number of global & generic memory read instructions executed on all compute units on the accelerator, per normalization unit.
The total number of global & generic memory write instructions executed on all compute units on the accelerator, per normalization unit.

The total number of spill/stack memory atomic (with and without return) instructions executed on all compute units on the accelerator, per normalization unit. Typically unused as these memory operations are typically used to implement thread-local storage.
The total number of spill/stack memory instructions executed on all compute units on the accelerator, per normalization unit.
The total number of spill/stack memory read instructions executed on all compute units on the accelerator, per normalization unit.
The total number of spill/stack memory write instructions executed on all compute units on the accelerator, per normalization unit.
The total number of memory instructions executed by the address processer over all compute units on the accelerator, per normalization unit.
The number of cycles the address processing unit spent working on coalesced spill/stack read instructions, per normalization unit.
The number of cycles the address processing unit spent working on coalesced spill/stack write instructions, per normalization unit.
The number of cycles the address processing unit spent working on spill/stack instructions, per normalization unit.

The number of atomic instructions submitted to the data-return unit by the address processor summed over all compute units on the accelerator, per normalization unit. This is expected to be the sum of global/generic and spill/stack atomics in the address processor.
Percent of the total CU cycles the data-return unit was stalled on data to be returned from the vL1D Cache RAM.
The number of instructions submitted to the data-return unit by the address processor that were found to be coalescable, per normalization unit.
Percent of the total CU cycles the data-return unit was busy processing or waiting on data to return to the CU.

The number of read instructions submitted to the data-return unit by the address processor summed over all compute units on the accelerator, per normalization unit. This is expected to be the sum of global/generic and spill/stack reads in the address processor.
Percent of the total CU cycles the data-return unit was stalled by the workgroup manager due to initialization of registers as a part of launching new workgroups.

The number of store instructions submitted to the data-return unit by the address processor summed over all compute units on the accelerator, per normalization unit. This is expected to be the sum of global/generic and spill/stack stores in the address processor.
MI300X.Command Processor (CPC/CPF) / Command pr: Percent of CPF busy cycles where the CPF was stalled for any reason.
Percent of total cycles where the CPF was busy actively doing any work. The ratio of CPF busy cycles over total cycles counted by the CPF.
Percent of CPF-L2 L2 busy cycles where the CPF-L2 interface was stalled for any reason.
Percent of total cycles counted by the CPF-L2 interface where the CPF-L2 interface was active doing any work. The ratio of CPF-L2 busy cycles over total cycles counted by the CPF-L2.
Percent of CPF busy cycles where the CPF was stalled by address translation.
Percent of CPC busy cycles spent decoding commands for processing.
Percent of CPC busy cycles where the CPC was stalled for any reason.
Percent of total cycles where the CPC was busy actively doing any work. The ratio of CPC busy cycles over total cycles counted by the CPC.
Percent of total cycles counted by the CPC-L2 interface where the CPC-L2 interface was active doing any work.
Percent of CPC busy cycles where the CPC was stalled by address translation
Percent of total cycles counted by the CPC's L2 address translation interface where the CPC was busy doing address translation work.
Percent of CPC busy cycles spent dispatching workgroups to the workgroup manager.
MI300X.Compute Units - Compute Pipeline / Arith: The total number of 16-bit brain floating-point operations executed on either the VALU or MFMA units, per normalization unit.
The total number of 16-bit floating-point operations executed on either the VALU or MFMA units, per normalization unit.
The total number of 32-bit floating-point operations executed on either the VALU or MFMA units, per normalization unit.
The total number of 64-bit floating-point operations executed on either the VALU or MFMA units, per normalization unit.
The total number of 8-bit floating-point MFMA operations executed, per normalization unit.
The total number of floating-point operations executed on either the VALU or MFMA units, per normalization unit.
The total number of 8-bit integer operations executed on either the VALU or MFMA units, per normalization unit.
The total number of integer operations executed on either the VALU or MFMA units, per normalization unit.
MI300X.Compute Units - Compute Pipeline / Compu: The total number of 16-bit brain floating point MFMA operations executed per second. Note: this does not include any 16-bit brain floating point operations from VALU instructions. This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical BF16 MFMA operations achievable on the specific accelerator.

The total number of 16-bit floating point MFMA operations executed per second. Note: this does not include any 16-bit floating point operations from VALU instructions. This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical F16 MFMA operations achievable on the specific accelerator.

The total number of 32-bit floating point MFMA operations executed per second. Note: this does not include any 32-bit floating point operations from VALU instructions. This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical F32 MFMA operations achievable on the specific accelerator.

The total number of 64-bit floating point MFMA operations executed per second. Note: this does not include any 64-bit floating point operations from VALU instructions. This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical F64 MFMA operations achievable on the specific accelerator.
The total number of 8-bit floating point MFMA operations executed per second. This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical F8 MFMA operations achievable on the specific accelerator.

The total number of 8-bit integer MFMA operations executed per second. Note: this does not include any 8-bit integer operations from VALU instructions. This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical INT8 MFMA operations achievable on the specific accelerator.

The total floating-point operations executed per second on the VALU. This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical FLOPs achievable on the specific accelerator. Note: this does not include any floating-point operations from MFMA instructions.
MI300X.Compute Units - Compute Pipeline / Pipel: Indicates what percent of the kernel's duration the branch unit was busy executing instructions. Computed as the ratio of the total number of cycles spent by the scheduler issuing branch instructions over the total CU cycles.
The ratio of the total number of instructions executed on the CU over the total active CU cycles.
The ratio of the total number of (non-internal) instructions issued over the number of cycles where the scheduler was actively working on issuing instructions.
The average duration of MFMA instructions in this kernel in cycles. Computed as the ratio of the total number of cycles the MFMA unit was busy over the total number of MFMA instructions.
Indicates what percent of the kernel's duration the MFMA unit was busy executing instructions. Computed as the ratio of the total number of cycles spent by the MFMA was busy over the total CU cycles.

Indicates what percent of the kernel's duration the SALU was busy executing instructions. Computed as the ratio of the total number of cycles spent by the scheduler issuing SALU / SMEM instructions over the total CU cycles.
The average number of round-trip cycles (that is, from issue to data return / acknowledgment) required for a SMEM instruction to complete.

Indicates the average level of divergence within a wavefront over the lifetime of the kernel. The number of work-items that were active in a wavefront during execution of each VALU instruction, time-averaged over all VALU instructions run on all wavefronts in the kernel

Indicates what percent of the kernel's duration the VALU was busy executing instructions. Does not include VMEM operations. Computed as the ratio of the total number of cycles spent by the scheduler issuing VALU instructions over the total CU cycles.
The average number of round-trip cycles (that is, from issue to data return / acknowledgment) required for a VMEM instruction to complete.

Indicates what percent of the kernel's duration the VMEM unit was busy executing instructions, including both global/generic and spill/scratch operations (see the VMEM instruction count metrics for more detail). Does not include VALU operations. Computed as the ratio of the total number of cycles spent by the scheduler issuing VMEM instructions over the total CU cycles.
MI300X.Compute Units - Instruction Mix / MFMA A: The total number of 16-bit brain floating point MFMA instructions issued per normalization unit.
The total number of 16-bit floating point MFMA instructions issued per normalization unit.
The total number of 32-bit floating-point MFMA instructions issued per normalization unit.
The total number of 64-bit floating-point MFMA instructions issued per normalization unit.
The total number of 8-bit floating point MFMA instructions issued per normalization unit. This is supported in AMD Instinct MI300 series and later only.
The total number of 8-bit integer MFMA instructions issued per normalization unit.
MI300X.Compute Units - Instruction Mix / Overal: The total number of branch operations issued. These typically consist of jump or branch operations and are used to implement control flow.
The total number of LDS (also known as shared memory) operations issued. These include loads, stores, atomics, and HIP's __shfl operations.
The total number of matrix fused multiply-add instructions issued.

The total number of scalar arithmetic logic unit (SALU) operations issued. Typically these are used for address calculations, literal constants, and other operations that are provably uniform across a wavefront. Although scalar memory (SMEM) operations are issued by the SALU, they are counted separately in this section.
The total number of scalar memory (SMEM) operations issued. These are typically used for loading kernel arguments, base-pointers and loads from HIP's __constant__ memory.

The total number of vector arithmetic logic unit (VALU) operations issued. These are the workhorses of the compute unit, and are used to execute a wide range of instruction types including floating point operations, non-uniform address calculations, transcendental operations, integer operations, shifts, conditional evaluation, etc.
The total number of vector memory operations issued. These include most loads, stores and atomic operations and all accesses to generic, global, private and texture memory.
MI300X.Compute Units - Instruction Mix / VALU A: The total number of type conversion instructions (such as converting data to or from F32\u2194F64) issued to the VALU per normalization unit.
The total number of addition instructions operating on 16-bit floating-point operands issued to the VALU per normalization unit.
The total number of fused multiply-add instructions operating on 16-bit floating-point operands issued to the VALU per normalization unit.
The total number of multiplication instructions operating on 16-bit floating-point operands issued to the VALU per normalization unit.
The total number of transcendental instructions (e.g., sqrt) operating on 16-bit floating-point operands issued to the VALU per normalization unit.
The total number of addition instructions operating on 32-bit floating-point operands issued to the VALU per normalization unit.
The total number of fused multiply-add instructions operating on 32-bit floating-point operands issued to the VALU per normalization unit.
The total number of multiplication instructions operating on 32-bit floating-point operands issued to the VALU per normalization unit.
The total number of transcendental instructions (such as sqrt) operating on 32-bit floating-point operands issued to the VALU per normalization unit.
The total number of addition instructions operating on 64-bit floating-point operands issued to the VALU per normalization unit.
The total number of fused multiply-add instructions operating on 64-bit floating-point operands issued to the VALU per normalization unit.
The total number of multiplication instructions operating on 64-bit floating-point operands issued to the VALU per normalization unit.
The total number of transcendental instructions (such as sqrt) operating on 64-bit floating-point operands issued to the VALU per normalization unit.
The total number of instructions operating on 32-bit integer operands issued to the VALU per normalization unit.
The total number of instructions operating on 64-bit integer operands issued to the VALU per normalization unit.
MI300X.Compute Units - Instruction Mix / VMEM I: The total number of global & generic memory atomic (with and without return) instructions executed on all compute units on the accelerator, per normalization unit.
The total number of global & generic memory instructions executed on all compute units on the accelerator, per normalization unit.
The total number of global & generic memory read instructions executed on all compute units on the accelerator, per normalization unit.
The total number of global & generic memory write instructions executed on all compute units on the accelerator, per normalization unit.

The total number of spill/stack memory atomic (with and without return) instructions executed on all compute units on the accelerator, per normalization unit. Typically unused as these memory operations are typically used to implement thread-local storage.
The total number of spill/stack memory instructions executed on all compute units on the accelerator, per normalization unit.
The total number of spill/stack memory read instructions executed on all compute units on the accelerator, per normalization unit.
The total number of spill/stack memory write instructions executed on all compute units on the accelerator, per normalization unit.
MI300X.Instruction Cache / L1I <-> L2 interface: Total number of bytes transferred across L1I - L2 interface divided by total duration.
MI300X.Instruction Cache / L1I Speed-of-Light /: The number of bytes looked up in the L1I cache, as a percent of the peak theoretical bandwidth. Calculated as the ratio of L1I requests over the total L1I cycles.
The percent of L1I requests that hit [#l1i-cache]_ on a previously loaded line the cache. Calculated as the ratio of the number of L1I requests that hit over the number of all L1I requests.

The percent of the peak theoretical L1I \u2192 L2 cache request bandwidth achieved. Calculated as the ratio of the total number of requests from the L1I to the L2 cache over the total L1I-L2 interface cycles.
MI300X.Instruction Cache / L1I cache accesses /: The percent of L1I requests that hit [#l1i-cache]_ on a previously loaded line the cache. Calculated as the ratio of the number of L1I requests that hit over the number of all L1I requests.
The total number of L1I requests that hit on a previously loaded cache line, per normalization-unit.
The average number of cycles spent to fetch instructions to a CU.
The total number of L1I requests that missed on a cache line that were already pending due to another request, per normalization-unit.
The total number of L1I requests that missed on a cache line that were not already pending due to another request, per normalization-unit.
The total number of requests made to the L1I per normalization-unit
MI300X.L2 Cache (per Channel) / Aggregate Stats: The percent of total number of requests to the L2 from all clients that hit in the cache. As noted in the Speed-of-Light section, this includes hit-on-miss requests.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 - Fabric Interface stalls: The number of cycles the L2-Fabric interface was stalled on write or atomic requests to any memory location because too many write/atomic requests were currently in flight, as a percent of the total active L2 cycles.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 - Fabric interface detaile: The total number of L2 requests to Infinity Fabric to atomically update 32B or 64B of data in any memory location, per normalization unit. See Request flow for more detail. Note that on current CDNA accelerators, such as the MI2XX, requests are only considered atomic by Infinity Fabric if they are targeted at non-write-cacheable memory, such as fine-grained memory allocations or uncached memory allocations on the MI2XX.
The total number of L2 requests to Infinity Fabric to read 32B or 64B of data from the accelerator's local HBM, per normalization unit.
The total number of L2 requests to Infinity Fabric to write or atomically update 32B or 64B of data in the accelerator's local HBM, per normalization unit.
The total number of L2 requests to Infinity Fabric to read 128B of data from any memory location, per normalization unit.
The total number of L2 requests to Infinity Fabric to read 32B of data from any memory location, per normalization unit.
The total number of L2 requests to Infinity Fabric to read 64B of data from any memory location, per normalization unit.

The total number of L2 requests to Infinity Fabric to read uncached data from any memory location, per normalization unit. 64B requests for uncached data are counted as two 32B uncached data requests.
The total number of L2 requests to Infinity Fabric to read 32B or 64B of data from any source other than the accelerator's local HBM, per normalization unit.
The total number of L2 requests to Infinity Fabric to write or atomically update 32B or 64B of data in any memory location other than the accelerator's local HBM, per normalization unit.
The total number of L2 requests to Infinity Fabric to write or atomically update 32B of data to any memory location, per normalization unit.
The total number of L2 requests to Infinity Fabric to write or atomically update 64B of data in any memory location, per normalization unit.
The total number of L2 requests to Infinity Fabric to write or atomically update 32B or 64B of uncached data, per normalization unit.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Cache Accesses / Atomic Re: The total number of atomic requests (with and without return) to the L2 from all clients.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Cache Accesses / Bandwidth: The number of bytes looked up in the L2 cache, divided by total duration. The number of bytes is calculated as the number of cache lines requested multiplied by the cache line size. This value does not consider partial requests, so for example, if only a single value is requested in a cache line, the data movement will still be counted as a full cache line.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Cache Accesses / CC Req: The total number of requests to the L2 that go to Coherently Cacheable (CC) memory allocations.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Cache Accesses / Cache Hit: The ratio of the number of L2 cache line requests that hit in the L2 cache over the total number of incoming cache line requests to the L2 cache.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Cache Accesses / Evict (In: The total number of L2 cache lines evicted from the cache due to capacity limits, per normalization unit.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Cache Accesses / Evict (vL: The total number of L2 cache lines evicted from the cache due to invalidation requests initiated by the vL1D cache, per normalization unit.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Cache Accesses / Hits: The total number of requests to the L2 from all clients that hit in the cache. As noted in the Speed-of-Light section, this includes hit-on-miss requests.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Cache Accesses / Misses: The total number of requests to the L2 from all clients that miss in the cache. As noted in the Speed-of-Light section, these do not include hit-on-miss requests.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Cache Accesses / NC Req: The total number of requests to the L2 to Not-hardware-Coherent (NC) memory allocations, per normalization unit.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Cache Accesses / Probe Req: The number of coherence probe requests made to the L2 cache from outside the accelerator. On an MI2XX, probe requests may be generated by, for example, writes to fine-grained device memory or by writes to coarse-grained device memory.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Cache Accesses / RW Req: The total number of requests to the L2 that go to Read-Write coherent memory (RW) allocations.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Cache Accesses / Read Req: The total number of read requests to the L2 from all clients.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Cache Accesses / Req: The total number of incoming requests to the L2 from all clients for all request types, per normalization unit.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Cache Accesses / Streaming: The total number of incoming requests to the L2 that are marked as streaming. The exact meaning of this may differ depending on the targeted accelerator, however on an MI2XX this corresponds to non-temporal load or stores. The L2 cache attempts to evict streaming requests before normal requests when the L2 is at capacity.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Cache Accesses / UC Req: The total number of requests to the L2 that go to Uncached (UC) memory allocations.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Cache Accesses / Write Req: The total number of write requests to the L2 from all clients.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Cache Accesses / Writeback: The total number of L2 cache lines written back to memory for any reason. Write-backs may occur due to user code (such as HIP kernel calls to _threadfence_system or atomic built-ins) by the command processor's memory acquire/release fences, or for other internal hardware reasons.
The total number of L2 cache lines written back to memory for internal hardware reasons, per normalization unit.
The total number of L2 cache lines written back to memory due to requests initiated by the vL1D cache, per normalization unit.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Speed-of-Light / HBM Bandw: Maximum theoretical bandwidth of the accelerator's local high-bandwidth memory (HBM) per unit time. This value is calculated as the number of HBM channels multiplied by the HBM channel width multiplied by the HBM clock frequency.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Speed-of-Light / Hit Rate: The ratio of the number of L2 cache line requests that hit in the L2 cache over the total number of incoming cache line requests to the L2 cache.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Speed-of-Light / L2-Fabric: The number of bytes read by the L2 over the Infinity Fabric interface per unit time.
The number of bytes sent by the L2 over the Infinity Fabric interface by write and atomic operations per unit time.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Speed-of-Light / Peak Band: The number of bytes looked up in the L2 cache, as a percent of the peak theoretical bandwidth achievable on the specific accelerator. The number of bytes is calculated as the number of cache lines requested multiplied by the cache line size. This value does not consider partial requests, so e.g., if only a single value is requested in a cache line, the data movement will still be counted as a full cache line.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2 Speed-of-Light / Utilizati: The ratio of the number of cycles an L2 channel was active, summed over all L2 channels on the accelerator over the total L2 cycles.
MI300X.L2 Cache / L2-Fabric interface metrics /: The time-averaged number of cycles atomic requests spent in Infinity Fabric before a completion acknowledgement (atomic without return value) or data (atomic with return value) was returned to the L2.

The percent of write requests generated by the L2 cache that are atomic requests to any memory location. This breakdown does not consider the size of the request (meaning that 32B and 64B requests are both counted as a single request), so this metric only approximates the percent of the L2-Fabric Read bandwidth directed to a remote location. Note that on current CDNA accelerators, such as the MI2XX, requests are only considered atomic by Infinity Fabric if they are targeted at fine-grained memory allocations or uncached memory allocations.

The percent of read requests generated by the L2 cache that are routed to the accelerator's local high-bandwidth memory (HBM). This breakdown does not consider the size of the request (meaning that 32B and 64B requests are both counted as a single request), so this metric only approximates the percent of the L2-Fabric Read bandwidth directed to the local HBM.

The percent of write and atomic requests generated by the L2 cache that are routed to the accelerator's local high-bandwidth memory (HBM). This breakdown does not consider the size of the request (meaning that 32B and 64B requests are both counted as a single request), so this metric only approximates the percent of the L2-Fabric Write and Atomic bandwidth directed to the local HBM. Note that on current CDNA accelerators, such as the MI2XX, requests are only considered atomic by Infinity Fabric if they are targeted at fine-grained memory allocations or uncached memory allocations.
The total number of bytes read by the L2 cache from Infinity Fabric divided by total duration.
The time-averaged number of cycles read requests spent in Infinity Fabric before data was returned to the L2.

The percent of read requests generated by the L2 cache that are routed to any memory location other than the accelerator's local high-bandwidth memory (HBM) - for example, the CPU's DRAM or a remote accelerator's HBM. This breakdown does not consider the size of the request (meaning that 32B and 64B requests are both counted as a single request), so this metric only approximates the percent of the L2-Fabric Read bandwidth directed to a remote location.

The percent of read requests generated by the L2 cache that are routed to any memory location other than the accelerator's local high-bandwidth memory (HBM) - for example, the CPU's DRAM or a remote accelerator's HBM. This breakdown does not consider the size of the request (meaning that 32B and 64B requests are both counted as a single request), so this metric only approximates the percent of the L2-Fabric Read bandwidth directed to a remote location. Note that on current CDNA accelerators, such as the MI2XX, requests are only considered atomic by Infinity Fabric if they are targeted at fine-grained memory allocations or uncached memory allocations.

The percent of read requests generated by the L2 cache that are reading from an uncached memory allocation. Note, as described in the request flow section, a single 64B read request is typically counted as two uncached read requests. So, it is possible for the Uncached Read Traffic to reach up to 200% of the total number of read requests. This breakdown does not consider the size of the request (i.e., 32B and 64B requests are both counted as a single request), so this metric only approximates the percent of the L2-Fabric read bandwidth directed to an uncached memory location.

The percent of write and atomic requests generated by the L2 cache that are targeting uncached memory allocations. This breakdown does not consider the size of the request (meaning that 32B and 64B requests are both counted as a single request), so this metric only approximates the percent of the L2-Fabric read bandwidth directed to uncached memory allocations.

The total number of bytes written by the L2 over Infinity Fabric by write and atomic operations divided by total duration. Note that on current CDNA accelerators, such as the MI2XX, requests are only considered atomic by Infinity Fabric if they are targeted at non-write-cacheable memory, for example, fine-grained memory allocations or uncached memory allocations on the MI2XX.
The time-averaged number of cycles write requests spent in Infinity Fabric before a completion acknowledgement was returned to the L2.
MI300X.Local Data Share (LDS) / LDS Speed-of-Li: Indicates the percentage of SIMDs in the VALU actively issuing LDS instructions, averaged over the lifetime of the kernel. Calculated as the ratio of the total number of cycles spent by the scheduler issuing LDS instructions over the total CU cycles.

Indicates the percentage of active LDS cycles that were spent servicing bank conflicts. Calculated as the ratio of LDS cycles spent servicing bank conflicts over the number of LDS cycles that would have been required to move the same amount of data in an uncontended access.

Indicates the maximum amount of bytes that could have been loaded from, stored to, or atomically updated in the LDS divided as percentage of theoretical peak. Does not take into account the execution mask of the wavefront when the instruction was executed.

Indicates what percent of the kernel's duration the LDS was actively executing instructions (including, but not limited to, load, store, atomic and HIP's __shfl operations). Calculated as the ratio of the total number of cycles LDS was active over the total CU cycles.
MI300X.Local Data Share (LDS) / LDS Statistics: The total number of cycles spent in the LDS scheduler due to address conflicts (as determined by the conflict resolution hardware) per normalization unit.
The total number of cycles spent on LDS atomics with return per normalization unit.
The total number of cycles spent in the LDS scheduler due to bank conflicts (as determined by the conflict resolution hardware) per normalization unit.

The ratio of the number of cycles spent in the LDS scheduler due to bank conflicts (as determined by the conflict resolution hardware) to the base number of cycles that would be spent in the LDS scheduler in a completely uncontended case. This is the unnormalized form of the Bank Conflict Rate.
The total number of cycles spent in the LDS scheduler over all operations per normalization unit.
The total number of LDS instructions (including, but not limited to, read/write/atomics and HIP's __shfl instructions) executed per normalization unit.
The average number of round-trip cycles (i.e., from issue to data-return acknowledgment) required for an LDS instruction to complete.
The total number of out-of-bounds accesses made to the LDS, per normalization unit. This is unused and expected to be zero in most configurations for modern CDNA\u2122 accelerators.

Indicates the maximum amount of bytes that could have been loaded from, stored to, or atomically updated in the LDS divided by total duration. Does not take into account the execution mask of the wavefront when the instruction was executed.
The total number of cycles spent in the LDS scheduler due to stalls from non-dword aligned addresses per normalization unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / Active CUs (deprecated): Total number of active compute units (CUs) on the accelerator during the kernel execution. (Deprecated - See CU Utilization instead)
MI300X.Memory Chart / BR: Total number of BRANCH instructions issued per normalization unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / Fabric Atomic Lat: The time-averaged number of cycles atomic requests spent in Infinity Fabric before a completion acknowledgement (atomic without return value) or data (atomic with return value) was returned to the L2.
MI300X.Memory Chart / Fabric Rd Lat: The time-averaged number of cycles read requests spent in Infinity Fabric before data was returned to the L2.
MI300X.Memory Chart / Fabric Wr Lat: The time-averaged number of cycles write requests spent in Infinity Fabric before a completion acknowledgement was returned to the L2.
MI300X.Memory Chart / Fabric_L2 Atomic: Number of L2 cache - Infinity Fabric write requests (either 32-byte or 64-byte) that are actually atomic requests summed over TCC instances per normalization unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / Fabric_L2 Rd: Number of L2 cache - Infinity Fabric read requests (either 32-byte or 64-byte) summed over TCC instances per normalization unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / Fabric_L2 Wr: Number of L2 cache - Infinity Fabric write requests (either 32-byte or 64-byte) summed over TCC instances per normalization unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / GWS: Total number of GDS (global data sync) instructions issued per normalization unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / HBM Rd: The total number of L2 requests to Infinity Fabric to read 32B or 64B of data from the accelerator's local HBM, per normalization unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / HBM Wr: The total number of L2 requests to Infinity Fabric to write or atomically update 32B or 64B of data in the accelerator's local HBM, per normalization unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / IL1 Fetch: The total number of requests made to the L1I per normalization-unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / IL1 Hit: The percent of L1I requests that hit on a previously loaded line the cache. Calculated as the ratio of the number of L1I requests that hit over the number of all L1I requests.
MI300X.Memory Chart / IL1 Lat: The average number of cycles spent to fetch instructions to a CU.
MI300X.Memory Chart / IL1_L2 Rd: The total number of requests across the L1I - L2 interface per normalization-unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / L2 Atomic: The total number of atomic requests (with and without return) to the L2 from all clients.
MI300X.Memory Chart / L2 Hit: The ratio of the number of L2 cache line requests that hit in the L2 cache over the total number of incoming cache line requests to the L2 cache.
MI300X.Memory Chart / L2 Rd: The total number of read requests to the L2 from all clients.
MI300X.Memory Chart / L2 Wr: The total number of write requests to the L2 from all clients.
MI300X.Memory Chart / LDS: The total number of LDS instructions (including, but not limited to, read/write/atomics and HIP's __shfl instructions) executed per normalization unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / LDS Allocation: The number of bytes of LDS memory (or, shared memory) allocated for this kernel. Note: This may also be larger than what was requested at compile time due to both allocation granularity and dynamic per-dispatch LDS allocations.
MI300X.Memory Chart / LDS Latency: The average number of round-trip cycles (i.e., from issue to data-return / acknowledgment) required for an LDS instruction to complete.
MI300X.Memory Chart / LDS Req: The total number of LDS instructions (including, but not limited to, read/write/atomics and HIP's __shfl instructions) executed per normalization unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / LDS Util: Indicates what percent of the kernel's duration the LDS was actively executing instructions (including, but not limited to, load, store, atomic and HIP's __shfl operations). Calculated as the ratio of the total number of cycles LDS was active over the total CU cycles.
MI300X.Memory Chart / Matrix Ops: Total number of MFMA (Matrix-Fused-Multiply-Add) instructions issued per normalization unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / Num CUs: Total number of compute units (CUs) on the accelerator.
MI300X.Memory Chart / SALU: Total Number of SALU (Scalar ALU) instructions issued per normalization unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / SGPR: The number of scalar general-purpose registers allocated for the kernel, see SALU. Note: this may not exactly match the number of SGPRs requested by the compiler due to allocation granularity.
MI300X.Memory Chart / SMEM: Total number of SMEM (Scalar Memory Read) instructions issued normalization unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / Scratch Allocation: The number of bytes of scratch memory requested per work-item for this kernel. Scratch memory is used for stack memory on the accelerator, as well as for register spills and restores.
MI300X.Memory Chart / VALU: The number of VALU (Vector ALU) instructions issued per normalization unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / VGPR: The number of architected vector general-purpose registers allocated for the kernel, see VALU. Note: this may not exactly match the number of VGPRs requested by the compiler due to allocation granularity.
MI300X.Memory Chart / VL1 Atomic: The total number of incoming atomic requests from the address processing unit after coalescing per normalization unit
MI300X.Memory Chart / VL1 Coalesce: Indicates how well memory instructions were coalesced by the address processing unit, ranging from uncoalesced (25%) to fully coalesced (100%). Calculated as the average number of thread-requests generated per instruction divided by the ideal number of thread-requests per instruction.
MI300X.Memory Chart / VL1 Hit: The ratio of the number of vL1D cache line requests that hit in vL1D cache over the total number of cache line requests to the vL1D Cache RAM.
MI300X.Memory Chart / VL1 Rd: The total number of incoming read requests from the address processing unit after coalescing per normalization unit
MI300X.Memory Chart / VL1 Stall: The ratio of the number of cycles where the vL1D is stalled waiting to issue a request for data to the L2 cache divided by the number of cycles where the vL1D is active.
MI300X.Memory Chart / VL1 Wr: The total number of incoming write requests from the address processing unit after coalescing per normalization unit
MI300X.Memory Chart / VL1_L2 Atomic: The number of atomic requests that are sent through the vL1D to the L2 cache, per normalization unit. This includes requests for atomics with, and without return.
MI300X.Memory Chart / VL1_L2 Rd: The number of read requests for a vL1D cache line that were not satisfied by the vL1D and must be retrieved from the to the L2 Cache per normalization unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / VL1_L2 Wr: The number of write requests to a vL1D cache line that were sent through the vL1D to the L2 cache, per normalization unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / VMEM: The number of VMEM (GPU Memory) read instructions issued (including FLAT/scratch memory) per normalization unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / Wave Life: Average number of cycles executing a wave.
MI300X.Memory Chart / Wavefronts: The total number of wavefronts, summed over all workgroups, forming this kernel launch.
MI300X.Memory Chart / Workgroups: The total number of workgroups forming this kernel launch.
MI300X.Memory Chart / sL1D Hit: The total number of sL1D requests that hit on a previously loaded cache line, per normalization unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / sL1D Lat: The average number of cycles scalar L1D cache requests spent in flight before data was returned to a CU.
MI300X.Memory Chart / sL1D Rd: The total number of requests, of any size or type, made to the sL1D per normalization unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / sL1D_L2 Atomic: The total number of atomic requests from sL1D to the L2, per normalization unit. Typically unused on current CDNA accelerators.
MI300X.Memory Chart / sL1D_L2 Rd: The total number of read requests from sL1D to the L2, per normalization unit.
MI300X.Memory Chart / sL1D_L2 Wr: The total number of write requests from sL1D to the L2, per normalization unit. Typically unused on current CDNA accelerators.
MI300X.Roofline / Roofline Performance Rates /: The total number of bytes read from and written to High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) per second. The peak empirically measured bandwidth achievable on the specific accelerator is displayed alongside for comparison.

The number of bytes looked up in the vL1D cache as a result of VMEM instructions per unit time. The number of bytes is calculated as the number of cache lines requested multiplied by the cache line size. This value does not consider partial requests, so e.g., if only a single value is requested in a cache line, the data movement will still be counted as a full cache line. The peak empirically measured bandwidth achievable on the specific accelerator is displayed alongside for comparison.

The number of bytes looked up in the L2 cache per unit time. The number of bytes is calculated as the number of cache lines requested multiplied by the cache line size. This value does not consider partial requests, so e.g., if only a single value is requested in a cache line, the data movement will still be counted as a full cache line. The peak empirically measured bandwidth achievable on the specific accelerator is displayed alongside for comparison.

Indicates the maximum amount of bytes that could have been loaded from, stored to, or atomically updated in the LDS per unit time (see LDS Bandwidth example for more detail). The peak empirically measured LDS bandwidth achievable on the specific accelerator is displayed alongside for comparison.

The total number of 16-bit brain floating point MFMA operations executed per second. Note: this does not include any 16-bit brain floating point operations from VALU instructions. The peak empirically measured BF16 MFMA operations achievable on the specific accelerator is displayed alongside for comparison.

The total number of 16-bit floating point MFMA operations executed per second. Note: this does not include any 16-bit floating point operations from VALU instructions. The peak empirically measured F16 MFMA operations achievable on the specific accelerator is displayed alongside for comparison.

The total number of 32-bit floating point MFMA operations executed per second. Note: this does not include any 32-bit floating point operations from VALU instructions. The peak empirically measured F32 MFMA operations achievable on the specific accelerator is displayed alongside for comparison.

The total number of 64-bit floating point MFMA operations executed per second. Note: this does not include any 64-bit floating point operations from VALU instructions. The peak empirically measured F64 MFMA operations achievable on the specific accelerator is displayed alongside for comparison.

The total number of 8-bit brain floating point MFMA operations executed per second. This does not include any 16-bit brain floating point operations from VALU instructions. The peak empirically measured F8 MFMA operations achievable on the specific accelerator is displayed alongside for comparison. It is supported on AMD Instinct MI300 series and later only.

The total number of 8-bit integer MFMA operations executed per second. Note: this does not include any 8-bit integer operations from VALU instructions. The peak empirically measured INT8 MFMA operations achievable on the specific accelerator is displayed alongside for comparison.

The total 16-bit floating-point operations executed per second on the VALU. This is presented with the value of the peak empirical F16 FLOPs achievable on the specific accelerator. Note: this does not include any F16 operations from MFMA instructions.

The total 32-bit floating-point operations executed per second on the VALU. This is presented with the value of the peak empirical F32 FLOPs achievable on the specific accelerator. Note: this does not include any F32 operations from MFMA instructions.

The total 64-bit floating-point operations executed per second on the VALU. This is presented with the value of the peak empirical F64 FLOPs achievable on the specific accelerator. Note: this does not include any F64 operations from MFMA instructions.
MI300X.Scalar L1 Data Cache / Scalar L1D Cache: The total number of atomic requests from sL1D to the L2, per normalization unit. Typically unused on current CDNA accelerators.
The total number of read requests from sL1D to the L2 per normalization unit.
The total number of cycles the sL1D\u2194L2 interface was stalled, per normalization unit.
The total number of write requests from sL1D to the L2, per normalization unit. Typically unused on current CDNA accelerators.

The total number of bytes read from, written to, or atomically updated across the sL1D\u2194L2 interface, divided by total duration. Note that sL1D writes and atomics are typically unused on current CDNA accelerators, so in the majority of cases this can be interpreted as an sL1D\u2192L2 read bandwidth.
MI300X.Scalar L1 Data Cache / Scalar L1D Speed-: The number of bytes looked up in the sL1D cache, as a percent of the peak theoretical bandwidth. Calculated as the ratio of sL1D requests over the total sL1D cycles.
Indicates the percent of sL1D requests that hit on a previously loaded line the cache. The ratio of the number of sL1D requests that hit over the number of all sL1D requests.
The percentage of the peak theoretical sL1D - L2 interface bandwidth acheived. Calculated as total number of bytes read from, written to, or atomically updated across the sL1D - L2 interface.
MI300X.Scalar L1 Data Cache / Scalar L1D cache: The total number of atomic requests from sL1D to the L2, per normalization unit. Typically unused on current CDNA accelerators.
Indicates the percent of sL1D requests that hit on a previously loaded line the cache. The ratio of the number of sL1D requests that hit over the number of all sL1D requests.
The total number of sL1D requests that hit on a previously loaded cache line, per normalization unit.
The total number of sL1D requests that missed on a cache line that was not already pending due to another request, per normalization unit.
The total number of sL1D requests that missed on a cache line that was already pending due to another request, per normalization unit.
The total number of sL1D read requests made for a single dword of data (4B), per normalization unit.
The total number of sL1D read requests made for a sixteen dwords of data (64B), per normalization unit.
The total number of sL1D read requests made for a two dwords of data (8B), per normalization unit.
The total number of sL1D read requests made for a four dwords of data (16B), per normalization unit.
The total number of sL1D read requests made for a eight dwords of data (32B), per normalization unit.
The total number of sL1D read requests of any size, per normalization unit.
The total number of requests, of any size or type, made to the sL1D per normalization unit.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / Active CUs (depr: Total number of active compute units (CUs) on the accelerator during the kernel execution. (Deprecated - See CU Utilization instead)
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / Branch Utilizati: Indicates what percent of the kernel's duration the branch unit was busy executing instructions. Computed as the ratio of the total number of cycles spent by the scheduler issuing branch instructions over the total CU cycles
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / CU Utilization: The percent of total SIMD cycles in the kernel where any SIMD on a CU was actively doing any work, summed over all CUs. Low values (less than 100%) indicate that the accelerator was not fully saturated by the kernel, or a potential load-imbalance issue.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / IPC: The ratio of the total number of instructions executed on the CU over the total active CU cycles. This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical bandwidth achievable on the specific accelerator.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / L1I BW: The percent of L1I requests that hit on a previously loaded line the cache. Calculated as the ratio of the number of L1I requests that hit over the number of all L1I requests.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / L1I Fetch Latenc: The average number of cycles spent to fetch instructions to a CU.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / L1I Hit Rate: The number of bytes looked up in the L1I cache per unit time. This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical bandwidth achievable on the specific accelerator.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / L2 Cache BW: The number of bytes looked up in the L2 cache per unit time. The number of bytes is calculated as the number of cache lines requested multiplied by the cache line size. This value does not consider partial requests, so e.g., if only a single value is requested in a cache line, the data movement will still be counted as a full cache line. This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical bandwidth achievable on the specific accelerator.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / L2 Cache Hit Rat: The ratio of the number of L2 cache line requests that hit in the L2 cache over the total number of incoming cache line requests to the L2 cache.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / L2-Fabric Read B: The number of bytes read by the L2 over the Infinity Fabric\u2122 interface per unit time. This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical bandwidth achievable on the specific accelerator.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / L2-Fabric Read L: The time-averaged number of cycles read requests spent in Infinity Fabric before data was returned to the L2.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / L2-Fabric Write: The number of bytes sent by the L2 over the Infinity Fabric interface by write and atomic operations per unit time. This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical bandwidth achievable on the specific accelerator.
The time-averaged number of cycles write requests spent in Infinity Fabric before a completion acknowledgement was returned to the L2.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / LDS Bank Conflic: The ratio of the number of cycles spent in the LDS scheduler due to bank conflicts (as determined by the conflict resolution hardware) to the base number of cycles that would be spent in the LDS scheduler in a completely uncontended case. This is also presented in normalized form (i.e., the Bank Conflict Rate).
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / MFMA FLOPs (BF16: The total number of 16-bit brain floating point MFMA operations executed per second. Note: this does not include any 16-bit brain floating point operations from VALU instructions. This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical BF16 MFMA operations achievable on the specific accelerator.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / MFMA FLOPs (F16): The total number of 16-bit floating point MFMA operations executed per second. Note: this does not include any 16-bit floating point operations from VALU instructions. This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical F16 MFMA operations achievable on the specific accelerator.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / MFMA FLOPs (F32): The total number of 32-bit floating point MFMA operations executed per second. Note: this does not include any 32-bit floating point operations from VALU instructions. This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical F32 MFMA operations achievable on the specific accelerator.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / MFMA FLOPs (F64): The total number of 64-bit floating point MFMA operations executed per second. Note: this does not include any 64-bit floating point operations from VALU instructions. This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical F64 MFMA operations achievable on the specific accelerator.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / MFMA FLOPs (F8): The total number of 8-bit brain floating point MFMA operations executed per second. This does not include any 16-bit brain floating point operations from VALU instructions. This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical F8 MFMA operations achievable on the specific accelerator. It is supported on AMD Instinct MI300 series and later only.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / MFMA IOPs (Int8): The total number of 8-bit integer MFMA operations executed per second. Note: this does not include any 8-bit integer operations from VALU instructions. This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical INT8 MFMA operations achievable on the specific accelerator.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / MFMA Utilization: Indicates what percent of the kernel's duration the MFMA unit was busy executing instructions. Computed as the ratio of the total number of cycles the MFMA was busy over the total CU cycles.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / SALU Utilization: Indicates what percent of the kernel's duration the SALU was busy executing instructions. Computed as the ratio of the total number of cycles spent by the scheduler issuing SALU or SMEM instructions over the total CU cycles.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / Theoretical LDS: Indicates the maximum amount of bytes that could have been loaded from, stored to, or atomically updated in the LDS per unit time (see LDS Bandwidth example for more detail). This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical F64 MFMA operations achievable on the specific accelerator.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / VALU Active Thre: Indicates the average level of divergence within a wavefront over the lifetime of the kernel. The number of work-items that were active in a wavefront during execution of each VALU instruction, time-averaged over all VALU instructions run on all wavefronts in the kernel.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / VALU FLOPs: The total floating-point operations executed per second on the VALU. This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical FLOPs achievable on the specific accelerator. Note: this does not include any floating-point operations from MFMA instructions.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / VALU Utilization: Indicates what percent of the kernel's duration the VALU was busy executing instructions. Does not include VMEM operations. Computed as the ratio of the total number of cycles spent by the scheduler issuing VALU instructions over the total CU cycles.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / VMEM Utilization: Indicates what percent of the kernel's duration the VMEM unit was busy executing instructions, including both global/generic and spill/scratch operations (see the VMEM instruction count metrics) for more detail). Does not include VALU operations. Computed as the ratio of the total number of cycles spent by the scheduler issuing VMEM instructions over the total CU cycles.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / Wavefront Occupa: The time-averaged number of wavefronts resident on the accelerator over the lifetime of the kernel. Note: this metric may be inaccurate for short-running kernels (less than 1ms). This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical occupancy achievable on the specific accelerator.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / sL1D Cache BW: The number of bytes looked up in the sL1D cache per unit time. This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical bandwidth achievable on the specific accelerator.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / sL1D Cache Hit R: The percent of sL1D requests that hit on a previously loaded line the cache. Calculated as the ratio of the number of sL1D requests that hit over the number of all sL1D requests.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / vL1D Cache BW: The number of bytes looked up in the vL1D cache as a result of VMEM instructions per unit time. The number of bytes is calculated as the number of cache lines requested multiplied by the cache line size. This value does not consider partial requests, so e.g., if only a single value is requested in a cache line, the data movement will still be counted as a full cache line. This is also presented as a percent of the peak theoretical bandwidth achievable on the specific accelerator.
MI300X.System Speed-of-Light / vL1D Cache Hit R: The ratio of the number of vL1D cache line requests that hit in vL1D cache over the total number of cache line requests to the vL1D cache RAM.
MI300X.Vector L1 Data Cache / L1 Unified Transl: The ratio of the number of translation requests that hit in the UTCL1 divided by the total number of translation requests made to the UTCL1.
The number of translation requests that hit in the UTCL1, and could be reused, per normalization unit.

The total number of translation requests that missed in the UTCL1 due to a permission error, per normalization unit. This is unused and expected to be zero in most configurations for modern CDNA\u2122 accelerators.
The number of translation requests made to the UTCL1 per normalization unit.
The total number of translation requests that missed in the UTCL1 due to translation not being present in the cache, per normalization unit.
MI300X.Vector L1 Data Cache / L1D - L2 Transact: Total atomic requests with CC mtype from this TCP to all TCCs Sum over TCP instances per normalization unit.
Total read requests with CC mtype from this TCP to all TCCs Sum over TCP instances per normalization unit.
Total write requests with CC mtype from this TCP to all TCCs Sum over TCP instances per normalization unit.
Total atomic requests with NC mtype from this TCP to all TCCs Sum over TCP instances per normalization unit.
Total read requests with NC mtype from this TCP to all TCCs Sum over TCP instances per normalization unit.
Total write requests with NC mtype from this TCP to all TCCs Sum over TCP instances per normalization unit.
Total atomic requests with RW mtype from this TCP to all TCCs Sum over TCP instances per normalization unit.
Total read requests with RW mtype from this TCP to all TCCs Sum over TCP instances per normalization unit.
Total write requests with RW mtype from this TCP to all TCCs Sum over TCP instances per normalization unit.
Total atomic requests with UC mtype from this TCP to all TCCs Sum over TCP instances per normalization unit.
Total read requests with UC mtype from this TCP to all TCCs Sum over TCP instances per normalization unit.
Total write requests with UC mtype from this TCP to all TCCs Sum over TCP instances per normalization unit.
MI300X.Vector L1 Data Cache / vL1D Speed-of-Lig: The number of bytes looked up in the vL1D cache as a result of VMEM instructions, as a percent of the peak theoretical bandwidth achievable on the specific accelerator. The number of bytes is calculated as the number of cache lines requested multiplied by the cache line size. This value does not consider partial requests, so for instance, if only a single value is requested in a cache line, the data movement will still be counted as a full cache line.

Indicates how well memory instructions were coalesced by the address processing unit, ranging from uncoalesced (25%) to fully coalesced (100%). Calculated as the average number of thread-requests generated per instruction divided by the ideal number of thread-requests per instruction.
The ratio of the number of vL1D cache line requests that hit in vL1D cache over the total number of cache line requests to the vL1D Cache RAM.

Indicates how busy the vL1D Cache RAM was during the kernel execution. The number of cycles where the vL1D Cache RAM is actively processing any request divided by the number of cycles where the vL1D is active.
MI300X.Vector L1 Data Cache / vL1D cache access: The total number of incoming atomic requests from the address processing unit after coalescing per normalization unit.
The total number of cache line lookups in the vL1D.

The number of bytes looked up in the vL1D cache as a result of VMEM instructions divided by total duration. The number of bytes is calculated as the number of cache lines requested multiplied by the cache line size. This value does not consider partial requests, so for instance, if only a single value is requested in a cache line, the data movement will still be counted as a full cache line.
The ratio of the number of vL1D cache line requests that hit in vL1D cache over the total number of cache line requests to the vL1D Cache RAM.
The number of cache accesses minus the number of outgoing requests to the L2 cache, that is, the number of cache line requests serviced by the vL1D Cache RAM per normalization unit.
The number of times the vL1D was issued a write-back invalidate command during the kernel's execution per normalization unit. This may be triggered by, for instance, the buffer_wbinvl1 instruction.
The number of atomic requests that are sent through the vL1D to the L2 cache, per normalization unit. This includes requests for atomics with, and without return.

The number of bytes transferred across the vL1D-L2 interface as a result of VMEM instructions, divided by total duration. The number of bytes is calculated as the number of cache lines requested multiplied by the cache line size. This value does not consider partial requests, so for instance, if only a single value is requested in a cache line, the data movement will still be counted as a full cache line.
The number of read requests for a vL1D cache line that were not satisfied by the vL1D and must be retrieved from the to the L2 Cache per normalization unit.
The number of write requests to a vL1D cache line that were sent through the vL1D to the L2 cache, per normalization unit.
The total number of incoming read requests from the address processing unit after coalescing per normalization unit.
The total number of incoming requests from the address processing unit after coalescing.
The total number of incoming write requests from the address processing unit after coalescing per normalization unit.
MI300X.Vector L1 Data Cache / vL1D cache stall: The ratio of the number of cycles where the vL1D is stalled waiting for requested data to return from the L2 cache divided by the number of cycles where the vL1D is active.
The ratio of the number of cycles where the vL1D is stalled waiting to issue a request for data to the L2 cache divided by the number of cycles where the vL1D is active.
The ratio of the number of cycles where the vL1D is stalled due to Atomic requests with conflicting tags being looked up concurrently, divided by the number of cycles where the vL1D is active.
The ratio of the number of cycles where the vL1D is stalled due to Read requests with conflicting tags being looked up concurrently, divided by the number of cycles where the vL1D is active.
The ratio of the number of cycles where the vL1D is stalled due to Write requests with conflicting tags being looked up concurrently, divided by the number of cycles where the vL1D is active.
MI300X.Wavefront / Wavefront Launch Stats / AGP: The number of accumulation vector general-purpose registers allocated for the kernel, see AGPRs. Note: this may not exactly match the number of AGPRs requested by the compiler due to allocation granularity.
MI300X.Wavefront / Wavefront Launch Stats / Gri: The total number of work-items (or, threads) launched as a part of the kernel dispatch. In HIP, this is equivalent to the total grid size multiplied by the total workgroup (or, block) size.
MI300X.Wavefront / Wavefront Launch Stats / LDS: The number of bytes of LDS memory (or, shared memory) allocated for this kernel. Note: This may also be larger than what was requested at compile time due to both allocation granularity and dynamic per-dispatch LDS allocations.
MI300X.Wavefront / Wavefront Launch Stats / Res: The total number of wavefronts restored from a context-save.
MI300X.Wavefront / Wavefront Launch Stats / SGP: The number of scalar general-purpose registers allocated for the kernel, see SALU. Note: this may not exactly match the number of SGPRs requested by the compiler due to allocation granularity.
MI300X.Wavefront / Wavefront Launch Stats / Sav: The total number of wavefronts saved at a context-save.
MI300X.Wavefront / Wavefront Launch Stats / Scr: The number of bytes of scratch memory requested per work-item for this kernel. Scratch memory is used for stack memory on the accelerator, as well as for register spills and restores.
MI300X.Wavefront / Wavefront Launch Stats / Tot: The total number of wavefronts launched as part of the kernel dispatch. On AMD Instinct\u2122 CDNA\u2122 accelerators and GCN\u2122 GPUs, the wavefront size is always 64 work-items. Thus, the total number of wavefronts should be equivalent to the ceiling of grid size divided by 64.
MI300X.Wavefront / Wavefront Launch Stats / VGP: The number of architected vector general-purpose registers allocated for the kernel, see VALU. Note: this may not exactly match the number of VGPRs requested by the compiler due to allocation granularity.
MI300X.Wavefront / Wavefront Launch Stats / Wor: The total number of work-items (or, threads) in each workgroup (or, block) launched as part of the kernel dispatch. In HIP, this is equivalent to the total block size.
MI300X.Wavefront / Wavefront Runtime Stats / Ac: The average number of cycles a wavefront in the kernel dispatch was actively executing instructions per normalization unit. This measurement is made on a per-wavefront basis, and may include cycles that another wavefront spent actively executing (on another execution unit, for example) or was stalled. As such, it is most useful to get a sense of how waves were spending their time, rather than identification of a precise limiter. The sum of this metric, Issue Wait Cycles and Active Wait Cycles should be equal to the total Wave Cycles metric.
MI300X.Wavefront / Wavefront Runtime Stats / De: The number of cycles a wavefront in the kernel dispatch spent resident on a compute unit per normalization unit. This is averaged over all wavefronts in a kernel dispatch.
MI300X.Wavefront / Wavefront Runtime Stats / In: The average number of instructions (of all types) executed per wavefront. This is averaged over all wavefronts in a kernel dispatch.
MI300X.Wavefront / Wavefront Runtime Stats / Is: The number of cycles a wavefront in the kernel dispatch was unable to issue an instruction for any reason (e.g., execution pipe back-pressure, arbitration loss, etc.) per normalization unit. This counter is incremented at every cycle by all wavefronts on a CU unable to issue an instruction. As such, it is most useful to get a sense of how waves were spending their time, rather than identification of a precise limiter because another wave could be actively executing while a wave is issue stalled. The sum of this metric, Dependency Wait Cycles and Active Cycles should be equal to the total Wave Cycles metric.
MI300X.Wavefront / Wavefront Runtime Stats / Ke: The total duration of the executed kernel.
The total duration of the executed kernel in cycles.
MI300X.Wavefront / Wavefront Runtime Stats / Wa: The number of cycles a wavefront in the kernel dispatch spent resident on a compute unit per normalization unit. This is averaged over all wavefronts in a kernel dispatch.
The time-averaged number of wavefronts resident on the accelerator over the lifetime of the kernel. Note: this metric may be inaccurate for short-running kernels (less than 1ms).
MI300X.Workgroup Manager (SPI) / Workgroup Mana: The percent of total CU cycles in the kernel where a workgroup could not be scheduled to a CU due to lack of available barriers.
The percent of total CU cycles in the kernel where a workgroup could not be scheduled to a CU due to lack of available LDS.
The percent of total SIMD cycles in the kernel where a workgroup could not be scheduled to a SIMD due to lack of available SGPRs.
The percent of total SIMD cycles in the kernel where a workgroup could not be scheduled to a SIMD due to lack of available VGPRs.
The percent of total SIMD cycles in the kernel where a workgroup could not be scheduled to a SIMD due to lack of available waveslots.

The percent of total scheduler-pipe cycles in the kernel where a workgroup could not be scheduled to a CU due to a bottleneck within the scheduler-pipes rather than a lack of a CU or SIMD with sufficient resources.

The percent of total scheduler-pipe cycles in the kernel where a workgroup could not be scheduled to a CU due to a bottleneck within the workgroup manager rather than a lack of a CU or SIMD with sufficient resources.

The percent of total CU cycles in the kernel where a wavefront could not be scheduled to a CU due to limits within the workgroup manager. This is expected to be always be zero on CDNA2 or newer accelerators (and small for previous accelerators).

The percent of total CU cycles in the kernel where a workgroup could not be scheduled to a CU due to limits within the workgroup manager. This is expected to be always be zero on CDNA2 or newer accelerators (and small for previous accelerators).
The percent of total scheduler-pipe cycles in the kernel where a workgroup could not be scheduled to a CU due to occupancy limitations (like a lack of a CU or SIMD with sufficient resources).

The percent of total shader-engine cycles in the kernel where a workgroup could not be scheduled to a CU due to lack of private (a.k.a., scratch) memory slots. While this can reach up to 100%, note that the actual occupancy limitations on a kernel using private memory are typically quite small (for example, less than 1% of the total number of waves that can be scheduled to an accelerator).
MI300X.Workgroup Manager (SPI) / Workgroup mana: The percent of cycles in the kernel where the accelerator was actively doing any work.
The total number of wavefronts, summed over all workgroups, forming this kernel launch.
The total number of workgroups forming this kernel launch.

The percent of total SIMD cycles in the kernel where any SIMD on a CU was actively doing any work, summed over all CUs. Low values (less than 100%) indicate that the accelerator was not fully saturated by the kernel, or a potential load-imbalance issue.
The percent of total scheduler-pipe cycles in the kernel where the scheduler-pipes were actively doing any work.

The percent of total shader engine cycles in the kernel where any CU in a shader-engine was actively doing any work, normalized over all shader-engines. Low values (e.g., << 100%) indicate that the accelerator was not fully saturated by the kernel, or a potential load-imbalance issue.
The percent of cycles in the kernel where the workgroup manager was actively doing any work.
